correctness.rationale: The theorem defines both signs and all four neighborhood memberships explicitly. The finite trace-separation lemma is a monotone refinement of at most k classes in each sign: add one symmetric-difference witness per unresolved collision, at most k-1 per sign, retaining the root. Once both signed operand families are trace-injective, the four new neighborhood functions are well-defined on observable sets and arbitrary elsewhere. A signed structural induction proves exact restriction of every subformula, including free negative Boolean and negation sets. The proposed 2k-1 trace lower example forces one independent point for each of k-1 positive and k-1 negative singleton operands, with the fixed root. Every finite signed certificate realizes a genuine model precisely because equal operand-sign columns induce equal modal-parent-sign columns for each operator; its size is polynomial. The classical hardness translation replaces classical negation with implication into a fresh falsified atom, and adjoining that atom disjoins away the other valuation case. Script output checks 2700 finite compressions, 1500 signed certificates, and 9600 truth assignments. Tests are not substituted for proofs.

originality.rationale: In the full-text 2026 source, the four independent signed modal neighborhood clauses are presented for semantics/completeness/correspondence, with no explicit bound on a root-preserving signed subformula model or polynomial columns for finite-premise consequence. Drobyshevich--Skurt 2021 treats stronger FDE truth operations and tests proof pairs, not separately free rejections in this CLoN syntax. Dalmonte--Olivetti--Negri 2018 proves finite model property for classically negated bi-neighborhood logic E but does not state the simultaneous signed trace bound 2k-1. Dalmonte--Mazzullo 2023 establishes the same abstract coNP class for classically negated nonnormal systems (Theorem 3), and thus the abstract complexity classification is NOT claimed as stand-alone novelty. The distinctive claim is explicit root-preserving polarity-by-polarity compression with sharp joint trace-separation budget and the exact corresponding certificate under the 2026 weak-negation semantics.
residual_risks: A general extensionality/finite-filtration theorem for multi-sorted modal neighborhoods could yield the same 2k-1 sign-preserving form under a translation not indexed by CLoN.
The 2023 classical coNP theorem already covers the abstract complexity class; only the signed structural preservation/concrete certificate supplies the distinctive contribution.
The stronger frame subclasses CLuN/CLaN and axiomatic neighborhood restrictions are outside the theorem; extrapolation would be unsound.
The original semantics is compared via the explicit four membership clauses; proof-pair-valued FDE models are not silently identified with single-sign membership models.

value.rationale: The 2026 bimodal weak-negation framework has independently chosen rejection sets for nonmodal compounds and independently specified positive and negative modal memberships. Ordinary one-signed filtrations cannot reconstruct weak-negation truth and negated modalities. The explicit simultaneous sign-preserving compression is a structural finite-model result with a sharp representation-level witness budget 2k-1. It supplies a polynomial certificate for finite-premise local semantic consequence on precisely this emergent semantics. This is motivated beyond a mere renaming of coNP for classical E and avoids unwarranted claims for stronger frame subclasses or optimal minimum model size.
